pdkit.stdout:
pdkit — deterministic helper for the Podman Desktop Kit plugin Usage: pdkit [options] Commands: init create $PDKIT_HOME and generate the package map doctor [--gate-selftest] check the environment; --gate-selftest drives every forbidden command through the real hook state show the state record state --to [--route ] move the issue, if the machine allows it; --route records what triage decided (standard, quickfix, multi-slice, redo) next one line: what to run next for this issue. For the start of a fresh session, which is where each phase now begins ids requirement|task|slice ALLOCATE the next ID and spend it — not a lookup. To see an issue's requirements run `state `; its tasks, `audit ` ids freeze freeze the requirement set ids branch --issue --slug [--index ] journal [--issue ] [--since ] [--event ] --since takes a date (2026-08-02) or an age (90m, 2h, 7d, 3w); anything else is refused. --event denied shows what the gate refused journal conflict --issue --kind mechanical|semantic --file

--resolution [--commit ] [--slice ] [--amendment A] record a conflict a rebase produced. The one entry a person writes: nothing can observe what upstream rewrote under a plan, and the two event names are the only ones this command will write packages [--of ] the package map, or the package owning a path issue list [--label a,b] [--limit ] open issues with the facts that say whether one can be started: linked pull requests, assignee, whether a maintainer answered, whether a bug carries a reproduction. An order, not a pick issue fetch [--full] read the upstream issue: the body whole, the newest triage.fetch_comments comments; --full prints them all issue history what was tried before: the merged pull request, what reverted it, what reviewers said, and what has happened in those files since. Required before the redo route may leave triage issue adopt --reason [--state ] [--pr ] [--branch ] [--route ] take work that predates the plugin into the machine: records what is true, marks the record adopted, and does not invent the artefacts of the states it never passed. Defaults to pr-open issue rework --reason the review rejected the approach: back to triage with the pull request left open. Planning runs from the issue, not from the diff that was refused issue escalate send a quickfix back to triage, so R-IDs come from the issue rather than from the diff issue block --by --reason this issue waits on another that must merge first: work a reviewer wants landed before this one, which this issue's slices cannot hold issue unblock --by [--reason ] what it waited on has landed, or stopped mattering issue draft-blocker --what [--pr ] [--raised-by ] [--url ] [--prior ] [--title ] draft the upstream issue for work that must merge before this one, into blockers/. Opening it is yours; then issue block with the number it got issue blocks [--check] [--all] what it waits on; --check reads each blocker's state from GitHub and lifts nothing branch create --issue --slug [--index ] render
